title: Chris and Guy Kelly, Alexis Rochon and a tenor player
summary: De De compares the Kelly brothers, Chris the any-job player and Guy the reader with Celestin, then names sax player Alexis Rochon.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: What about Chris Kelly? Who did he have in his band? Do you remember any of those fellas at all?

No. Chris had so many of them. What about Guy Kelly? Do you remember any of the fellas? I did. His brother, well he worked with Papa Celestine a lot. He was, in other words, played second with Papa Celestine most of the time. What did you say about his brother?
Chris? Yeah. Didn't you say something about brother and Guy there?

Oh, they were two brothers, yeah, quite natural. But Guy Kelly, yeah, oh yeah, they were brothers. But Guy Kelly was more musical, you know, reading man. Read more. That's how he stayed more with Papa Celestine. But Chris was just actually anywhere, any little job, three pieces, four pieces, he would get to play it. But they claim he knew a lot of music. He never played it though. I was told he read red, red, yeah, red, nice. He got out of the story. What about this fella, Rochon, you mentioned
the other day? Alexis. Is that his name, Alexis Rochon? Alexis Rochon. And what instrument did he play?
Sax. He was a good man on the sax. And who was this guy, Wright, that played tenor sax? He was a couple by Tredd, he played tenor sax or something. What was it coming in?
Remember his first name? Maybe Alba.

Maybe Alba, huh? You're not sure. I'm not sure. I'm going to it with Alba doing. I think so. I know he's becoming here. We were talking about him this morning, wasn't it? The other day, Rochon. The other day. We were talking about Rochon. Rochon, he's a preacher now, he's out of it too.
